RELG 101.description: Beliefs and practices of the world's religions and the methods scholars use to study them.
RELG 101.subject: RELG
RELG 101.title: Exploring Religion

RELG 120.description: Issues, theories, and debates that shape global religious traditions, cultures, and communities; examination of historical contexts and development, applying social scientific inquiry and methods to analyze relevant current circumstances and concerns.
RELG 120.subject: RELG
RELG 120.title: Comparative Religion

RELG 201.description: Exploration of the dynamic relationships between selected religions and cultures.
RELG 201.subject: RELG
RELG 201.title: Religion and Culture

RELG 202.description: Critical study of the intellectual strands leading to Western disconnections between reason and faith; the search for balance between belief and reason with emphasis on contemporary developments.
RELG 202.subject: RELG
RELG 202.title: Introduction to Reason and Faith

RELG 204.description: The diversity of religious traditions in America.
RELG 204.subject: RELG
RELG 204.title: Introduction to Religions in America

RELG 205.description: Values and ethics as developed, contested, and transmitted through a variety of religious practices.
RELG 205.subject: RELG
RELG 205.title: Morality, Ethics, and Religion

RELG 206.description: A survey of the beliefs and practices associated with the demonic and the Devil from c 500 B.C.E. to the 20th century.
RELG 206.subject: RELG
RELG 206.title: History of the Devil

RELG 207.description: The variety of religious traditions of African Americans, with emphasis on the contexts in which they developed.
RELG 207.subject: RELG
RELG 207.title: Introduction to African American Religions

RELG 208.description: The fundamental elements of human culture as it relates to biblical archaeology. The defining characteristics of different kinds of society through interdependency of language and culture. The affects of modern world interests in defining / redefining this area.
RELG 208.subject: RELG
RELG 208.title: Biblical Archaeology

RELG 209.description: History of magic as theory and practice from antiquity to modernity and beyond. Chronological, geographical, and thematic range stretches from ancient Mesopotamia, Greece, and Rome; to the Jewish, Christian, and Islamic worlds; to early modernity and the modern period in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
RELG 209.subject: RELG
RELG 209.title: History of Magic

RELG 210.description: An interdisciplinary examination of the complexity of the Hindu religious and philosophical traditions covering such topics as deity, self, cosmos, body ritual, karma, and yoga.
RELG 210.subject: RELG
RELG 210.title: Introduction to Hinduism

RELG 219.description: Fundamental questions of ethical and moral inquiry in the religious traditions of Asia.
RELG 219.subject: RELG
RELG 219.title: Ethics and the Good Life in Asian Religions

RELG 220.description: An introduction to Buddhism from a social historical perspective that examines Buddhist religious goals, ethics, values, and practices in the local contexts of India, Sri Lanka, Tibet, China, and Japan.
RELG 220.subject: RELG
RELG 220.title: Introduction to Buddhism

RELG 221.description: Buddhist methods of meditation, asceticism, and similar disciplinary practices for personal and social transformation. Examination of classic Buddhist works from diverse cultures with attention to modern American practices.
RELG 221.subject: RELG
RELG 221.title: Buddhist Meditation in Theory and Practice

RELG 230.description: Overview of Jewish experiences, beliefs, practices from a contextual point of view.
RELG 230.subject: RELG
RELG 230.title: Introduction to Judaism

RELG 240.description: Introduction to the Christian religion, with emphasis on the history of the major traditions and movements that have shaped the multicultural practices and social impact of modern global Christianity.
RELG 240.subject: RELG
RELG 240.title: Introduction to Christianity

RELG 250.description: Interpretation of primary materials reflecting many dimensions of the Islamic religious tradition, such as the Qur'an, Hadith, legal, and theological and mystical writings, art, rituals, and contemporary Muslim voices.
RELG 250.subject: RELG
RELG 250.title: Introduction to Islam

RELG 260.description: A comparative examination of such topics as ritual, cosmology, revitalization movements, magic, witchcraft, myth, and possession.
RELG 260.subject: RELG
RELG 260.title: Anthropology of Magic and Religion

RELG 261.description: The human experience and expression of what it means to be religious.
RELG 261.subject: RELG
RELG 261.title: Global Human Religiosity

RELG 270.description: Literary, visual, and/or performance art associated with religious discourse and practice.
RELG 270.subject: RELG
RELG 270.title: Religion and the Arts

RELG 291.description: Special topics in Religious Studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
RELG 291.subject: RELG
RELG 291.title: Special Topics in Religious Studies

RELG 301.description: Modern study of the Hebrew Bible from historical, literary, and archeological points of view. Reading and analysis of texts in translation.
RELG 301.subject: RELG
RELG 301.title: Hebrew Bible (Old Testament)

RELG 302.description: Historical and critical study of the New Testament writings, with emphasis on origins, production, and transmission.
RELG 302.subject: RELG
RELG 302.title: New Testament

RELG 310.description: Paul’s teachings and practices, as shown in his letters and how these resemble those of various cultural formations of his time, with emphasis on moral teachings and schools of Hellenistic philosophy.
RELG 310.subject: RELG
RELG 310.title: Paul and the Philosophers

RELG 311.description: Gospels about Jesus from the 1st and 2nd centuries CE; analysis with attention to canonical texts as well as those not contained in today’s major canonical collections; assessment of gospel literature in competing configurations of Christianity during its formative years.
RELG 311.subject: RELG
RELG 311.title: Gospel Literature and the Formation of Christianity

RELG 312.description: A critical study in the life and thought of Paul, his letters to the early Christian churches, his role in the expansion of the Christian movement, and his continuing influence today.
RELG 312.subject: RELG
RELG 312.title: The Life and Letters of Paul

RELG 314.description: The impact of religion on modern Western culture and, in turn, of culture on religion. Selected topics: Holocaust, Puritanism, fundamentalism, Islam, Freud, love wisdom tradition, civil religion.
RELG 314.subject: RELG
RELG 314.title: Religion and Culture

RELG 315.description: Christianity in the 1st through 5th centuries; its formation as seen through the literature of early Christians and their detractors.
RELG 315.subject: RELG
RELG 315.title: Early Christianity

RELG 316.description: Conceptions and representations of Jesus in antiquity up to the present; including the gospel traditions as well as literature, art, and film.
RELG 316.subject: RELG
RELG 316.title: Imagining Jesus: Antiquity to Present

RELG 320.description: Readings in the Gospels and Epistles.
RELG 320.subject: RELG
RELG 320.title: The Greek New Testament

RELG 321.description: Prophets, prophetic speech, and prophetic literature from the Hebrew Bible until today; their literary, sociological, and historical contexts; and the reception and interpretation of prophecy.
RELG 321.subject: RELG
RELG 321.title: Prophets and Prophecy

RELG 332.description: Basic Christian teachings concerning God, creation, sin, the person and work of Christ, and life after death.
RELG 332.subject: RELG
RELG 332.title: Christian Theology

RELG 333.description: Gender and sexuality in the shaping of social and individual identity in religious contexts.
RELG 333.subject: RELG
RELG 333.title: Sex, Gender, and Religion

RELG 334.description: A historical overview and critical introduction to the philosophical practices of Asian religions; an examination of the basic worldviews, thought frameworks, and foundational questions of the main schools of premodern Asian religious philosophy.
RELG 334.subject: RELG
RELG 334.title: Asian Religious Philosophy

RELG 335.description: Basic Christian teachings concerning human nature and conduct; historical foundations and contemporary applications.
RELG 335.subject: RELG
RELG 335.title: Christian Ethics

RELG 336.description: Historical, contextual, and developmental aspects of social justice as a significant function of religion.
RELG 336.subject: RELG
RELG 336.title: Social Justice Religion

RELG 337.description: Relationships between religion and the structure, institutions, and content of a nation’s political processes.
RELG 337.subject: RELG
RELG 337.title: Religion and Politics

RELG 338.description: Religion isn’t just personal—it shapes politics, communities, health, and relationships. Examine how religion interacts with culture and society, and how society shapes religion.
RELG 338.subject: RELG
RELG 338.title: Religion and Sociology

RELG 339.description: The study of the role of law, legal argumentation, and legal contexts in one or more religious traditions.
RELG 339.subject: RELG
RELG 339.title: Law and Religious Traditions

RELG 340.description: The worship of Yahweh and other deities in ancient Israel with special attention to the evolution of monotheism.
RELG 340.subject: RELG
RELG 340.title: God and the Gods

RELG 343.description: Explore development/theologies of African/African Diaspora religions; examine misunderstandings; arrive at a more sophisticated and nuanced vision of these religions and the people who hold them.
RELG 343.subject: RELG
RELG 343.title: Religions of the African Diaspora

RELG 344.description: One of the main paths to the divine in the Hindu tradition; deep devotion to a god or goddess, or bhakti, with expressions in art, poetry, mythology, theology, and ascetic fervor.
RELG 344.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: At least one 100- or 200-level Religious Studies course.
RELG 344.subject: RELG
RELG 344.title: Hindu Devotional Traditions

RELG 349.description: Investigation of the Buddhist and Hindu religious ideas and practices known as tantra. Topics include tantric views of the human body, freedom, and consciousness; tantric use of sec, imagination, visualization, and manipulation of bodily energy; role of tantric traditions in south Asian religions and cultures.
RELG 349.subject: RELG
RELG 349.title: Tantra: Sex, Power, and Bliss in South Asian Religions

RELG 350.description: Buddhist stories, poetry, novels, and films from various cultures and times examined for how they creatively convey their religious ideals. Study of great works of Buddhist writing, in English translation, analyzing their techniques and examining how Buddhists use film today for similar aims.
RELG 350.subject: RELG
RELG 350.title: Buddhist Stories, Poetry, and Films

RELG 351.description: Examination of major South Asian religions--Hinduism, Jainism, Buddhism, and Islam, emphasizing the historical context for changing religious ideals, and the commingling of traditions.
RELG 351.subject: RELG
RELG 351.title: Yoga: The Art of Spiritual Transformation

RELG 352.description: Expansion of Buddhism beyond India, development of Confucianism, Taoism, Shinto, and other national religious expressions in China and Japan.
RELG 352.subject: RELG
RELG 352.title: Religions of East Asia

RELG 354.description: The religious, political, social and economic institutions and intellectual and scholarly traditions developed by Muslim societies throughout Afro-Eurasia from late antiquity to the present.
RELG 354.subject: RELG
RELG 354.title: Islamic Institutions and Traditions

RELG 358.description: Intensive study of the Qur'an and Hadith: its major themes and literary quality, with attention to a range of classical and contemporary discourses about the Qur'an, both Islamic and Western.
RELG 358.subject: RELG
RELG 358.title: The Qur'an and Hadith

RELG 359.description: Close reading and discussion of primary texts (the Qur'an, Hadith, creeds, classical theological arguments, and modern writings) on major theological problems such as salvation, God, revelation, and religious pluralism.
RELG 359.subject: RELG
RELG 359.title: Islamic Theology and Philosophical Thought

RELG 361.description: The development of the religious consciousness and its various expressions, the psychological dynamics of growth and conversion, response to crisis, and the relation of spiritual practice to health and wholeness.
RELG 361.subject: RELG
RELG 361.title: Psychology of Religion

RELG 362.description: Occultism as a link between science and religion and its central role in Western intellectual and cultural history; the historical development of the science-magic-religion continuum in the Islamo-Christian world from late antiquity to present.
RELG 362.subject: RELG
RELG 362.title: Science, Magic and Religion

RELG 363.description: Examines the work of a range of living Muslim-American thinkers.
RELG 363.subject: RELG
RELG 363.title: American Islamic Thought

RELG 367.description: A survey of Islamic mysticism, its foundation in the Quranic revelation doctrines and practices, subsequent development, significance within Islamic civilization, and role in the contemporary world, both Islamic and non-Islamic.
RELG 367.subject: RELG
RELG 367.title: Sufism

RELG 368.description: Representative messianic movements, millenarian visionaries and apocalyptic imaginings in the Islamic world from the 7th century to the present, with attention to related developments in the Jewish and Christian traditions over the last two millennia.
RELG 368.subject: RELG
RELG 368.title: Messiahs, Mystics and Rebels in the Islamic World

RELG 369.description: Close reading and discussion of primary texts (scriptural, classical, and modern) and accounts of court cases, focuses on one aspect of Islamic law such as equity, violence, authority, or gender.
RELG 369.subject: RELG
RELG 369.title: Islamic Law

RELG 372.description: Existentialist thought as adapted by theologians to interpret religious experience and the biblical message. The movement from philosophical protest against essentialism into imaginative description of existence revealed under stress.
RELG 372.subject: RELG
RELG 372.title: Religion and Existentialism

RELG 373.description: Film, poetry and literature created in response to the Holocaust as the means for a decades long cultural discussion, in European and American societies, of the moral and religious implications of the Holocaust on our self-understandings as religious and moral beings.
RELG 373.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENGL 101 and ENGL 102.
RELG 373.subject: RELG
RELG 373.title: Literature and Film of the Holocaust

RELG 374.description: Regional faith traditions in Southern historical-cultural context: evangelical piety, denominational tradition, revival, African-American church, Lost Cause idealism.
RELG 374.subject: RELG
RELG 374.title: Religion in the South

RELG 377.description: Classic literary works from one or more religious traditions which have shaped and/or expressed the core ethos of a religious tradition or of the more general human concern for the religious and spiritual; and/or general literature (fiction, poetry, plays, essays, non-fiction) which incorporates religious or spiritual references, ideas, symbolism, allusions.
RELG 377.subject: RELG
RELG 377.title: Religion and Literature

RELG 381.description: The religious, cultural, social, and political conditions that shaped the Jewish experience in the Near East and Europe from Late Antiquity to 1500.
RELG 381.subject: RELG
RELG 381.title: Jewish History I: Late Antiquity to 1500

RELG 382.description: Case studies of Jewish history in Europe, America, and the land of Israel, 1500 to the present.
RELG 382.subject: RELG
RELG 382.title: Jewish History II: 1500 to the Present

RELG 387.description: Jewish-Muslim relations in the Near East and the US; an exploration of Jewish-Muslim encounters, issues of religious law, politics, radical religious ideologies, and their repercussions for today.
RELG 387.subject: RELG
RELG 387.title: Jews and Muslims

RELG 388.description: Historical investigation of kabbalah, a philosophical system and mystical current common to Judaism, Islam, and Christianity, from the medieval period to the present; focus on its formative role in early modern Western cosmology and science, and its ecological implications today.
RELG 388.subject: RELG
RELG 388.title: Kabbalah: Science, Religion and Nature in Western History

RELG 390.description: A historical overview of major theories and approaches in the academic study of religion.
RELG 390.subject: RELG
RELG 390.title: Theories of Religion

RELG 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
RELG 399.subject: RELG
RELG 399.title: Independent Study

RELG 410.description: Greek and Roman ethical theory, its adaptation into Judean and Christian traditions and impact on Western models of morality.
RELG 410.subject: RELG
RELG 410.title: Origins of Western Morality

RELG 412.description: Judeo-Christian views of God; modern criticism and contemporary responses.
RELG 412.subject: RELG
RELG 412.title: Faith, Doubt, and God

RELG 471.description: Conceptualization of race and its transformative impact on the study of religion; genealogical, historical, and theoretical parameters of the intersection between race and religion; recent scholarship that combines the categories of race and religion in the context of various religious communities.
RELG 471.subject: RELG
RELG 471.title: Race and Religion

RELG 472.description: Relationships between religion and science, especially considering impacts of mutual responses and questions with respect to human life in the 21st century.
RELG 472.subject: RELG
RELG 472.title: Religion and Science: Human Questions

RELG 473.description: Inter-relationships between religion, medicines, and healing; examining perspectives and practices, interfaces and influences across cultures.
RELG 473.subject: RELG
RELG 473.title: Religions, Medicines, and Healing

RELG 474.description: Contemporary and historical life-stories about spiritual or religious figures as presented in various forms such as biography, autobiography, hagiography, art, and/or film; explores both the specific issues within unique accounts and idealized, general models for spiritual lives.
RELG 474.subject: RELG
RELG 474.title: Spiritual Lives

RELG 475.description: Symbolic visions, tours of heaven and hell, cosmic battles, divine judgment, messianic figures, prophecy, or other forms of revelation as found in literature, art, or social movements from diverse geographical and historical locations.
RELG 475.subject: RELG
RELG 475.title: Visions of Apocalypse

RELG 488.description: Build an understanding of the contexts of religious studies; participate in ongoing scholarly discussions; and expand the serious student’s skills in critically analyzing religions.
RELG 488.subject: RELG
RELG 488.title: Perspective in Religious Studies

RELG 491.description: Advanced special topics in Religious Studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
RELG 491.subject: RELG
RELG 491.title: Advanced Special Topics in Religious Studies

RELG 492.description: Focused research on special topics in Religious Studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
RELG 492.subject: RELG
RELG 492.title: Special Topics in Research in Religious Studies

RELG 498.description: A supervised research project or other creative work, required of intensive majors, to be completed in the senior year.
RELG 498.subject: RELG
RELG 498.title: Advanced Project

RELG 551.description: Islam as a dynamic cultural tradition: emphasis on the tension between Islamization and the larger Islamic tradition.
RELG 551.subject: RELG
RELG 551.title: Tradition and Transformations in Islamic Cultures

RELG 700.description: Introduction to formative thinkers in the discipline of religious studies, with attention to the methodological problems of comparison.
RELG 700.subject: RELG
RELG 700.title: Problems in the Comparative Study of Religion

RELG 701.description: Foundational texts appropriate to the student's area of specialization and required for advanced course work and thesis preparation.
RELG 701.subject: RELG
RELG 701.title: Foundational Readings

RELG 710.description: Examination of the four major New Testament titles: Son of Man, Christ, Lord, and Son of God. Attention also given to some lesser-known titles and to Christology in context.
RELG 710.subject: RELG
RELG 710.title: The Christology of the New Testament

RELG 724.description: Religion as a factor in the comparative politics and international relations of states and societies.
RELG 724.subject: RELG
RELG 724.title: Religion and Politics

RELG 740.description: Beliefs and practices in ancient Israelite religion, with particular attention to the emergence of monotheism. Comparison with other ancient Near Eastern religions.
RELG 740.subject: RELG
RELG 740.title: Israelite Religion

RELG 760.description: Introduction to historical and contemporary approaches to the cross-disciplinary study of the inter-relations of the religious and the literary imaginations.
RELG 760.subject: RELG
RELG 760.title: Religion and Literature

RELG 770.description: Elements in the religion of the black slave in early America, the development of black churches and theological movements.
RELG 770.subject: RELG
RELG 770.title: Black Christianity in America

RELG 771.description: Tenets, themes, and representative figures in black and liberation theology in the United States and in Central and South America.
RELG 771.subject: RELG
RELG 771.title: Black and Liberation Theology

RELG 772.description: The diverse heritage of American evangelism, with special emphasis on its socio-political and theological origins in the late 18th and 19th centuries.
RELG 772.subject: RELG
RELG 772.title: Nineteenth-Century American Evangelical Thought

RELG 773.description: Various 20th-century christological perspectives, with special emphasis on the person and work of Jesus as bases for addressing life/death and hope/despair issues.
RELG 773.subject: RELG
RELG 773.title: Twentieth-Century Christology

RELG 780.description: An examination of the perennialist approach to the mystical and contemplative teachings of the major religious traditions.
RELG 780.subject: RELG
RELG 780.title: World Spirituality

RELG 789.description: Examination of contemporary problems in the philosophical foundations of religion.
RELG 789.subject: RELG
RELG 789.title: Seminar in Philosophical Theology

RELG 792.description: Topics related to the study of texts in the life of specific religious communities. Course content varies; individual topics will be announced.
RELG 792.subject: RELG
RELG 792.title: Special Topics in Texts and Traditions

RELG 793.description: Topics related to the study of religious doctrines, cosmologies, spiritual practices, and ethics. Course content varies; individual topics will be announced.
RELG 793.subject: RELG
RELG 793.title: Special Topics in Theology and Religious Thought

RELG 794.description: Topics examining religious institutions, practices, and experiences in relation to other cultural forms. Course content varies; individual topics will be announced.
RELG 794.subject: RELG
RELG 794.title: Special Topics in Religion and Society
